provider_mapping: Map to Cloudflare Cache Rules/Tiered Cache, Fastly cache configuration, CloudFront cache policies, or Azure Front Door caching after provider and plan review.

rules.match: GET/HEAD requests for versioned CSS, JavaScript, fonts, images and other immutable static assets
rules.cache_key: scheme + host + normalized path + relevant query parameters only
rules.notes: Increase TTL only when filenames/content are versioned. Never include untrusted forwarding headers in the cache key.

rules.match: GET/HEAD HTML documents on the public static hostname
rules.notes: Short edge TTL keeps GitHub Pages deployments responsive. Purge changed HTML after rollback when necessary.

rules.match: authentication, account, checkout, admin, webhook, personalized API, Set-Cookie or Authorization-bearing responses
rules.notes: Application Cache-Control remains authoritative for sensitive responses. Do not cache merely because the edge can.
Only cache API routes with an explicit route contract, stable cache key, CORS review and no user-specific data.

origin_shielding.github_pages: Use provider CDN caching to reduce ordinary origin requests, but do not describe this as private origin shielding; GitHub Pages cannot authenticate the edge.
origin_shielding.future_private_origin: Enable tiered/origin shielding only after the origin supports authenticated pulls, provider egress allowlists, mTLS, private connectivity or an equivalent access-control mechanism.

cache_poisoning_controls: Do not key on X-Forwarded-Host or other untrusted forwarding headers.
Normalize or explicitly select query parameters used by cached content.
Bypass responses with Set-Cookie, private, no-store or user-specific semantics.
Validate Host at the edge and application/origin where supported.
Test two clean requests after every cache-rule change and compare content, status, Age/cache-status and security headers.
